source_request: 시각 의미 데이터와 후보 데이터에 반영해줘. 그 다음 스킬의 최신 버전을 사용하여 독립된 서브에이전트 3개에서 각각 서로 다른 컨셉으로 이번에 반영한 주제가 이미지에 실제로 반영되는지까지 테스트할 수 있는 랜덤한 복잡한 컨셉을 정하여 테스트케이스를 마련하고 첨부한 이미지를 활용하여 프롬프트 작성하고 이미지 생성하도록 하여 잘 반영되었는지 테스트해줘.
interpreted_intent: The current requester context identifies the reflected research topic as soil and earth. The exact active request asks for a distinct random complex concept and use of the attached reference. A seeded independent draw chose an earth-pigment restoration workbench. The agent-invented circumstance is a fragile, flaking earthen relief being repaired using the same raw earth processed into wet filler. A viewer should connect the dry broken corner to the deliberate blade contact and an already bridged damp seam, with the worker’s attention and softened face suggesting tentative relief. The powder, clods, wet paste and transferred residue form material stages of one soil-centered task. These are agent-owned staging and test expectations, not requester definitions or extra material hard assertions. The visible reference face and dark bob inform appearance only; the worker’s role, feelings and history are fictional. Saved sensual 1 supports an understated intimate human warmth through facial presence, sleeveless cotton and hair near the cheek; fetish 0, surreal 0 and creativity 1 keep an ordinary, restrained workshop interpretation. All candidate access remains deferred until this independent baseline is frozen.
subject: A fictional woman with the visible reference face proportions and dark chin-length bob, working with an earthen-plaster relief.
setting: A small indoor daylight atelier with a scarred workbench, padded support and a compact raw-earth processing area.
event: An earth restoration in progress: dry damaged substrate, current palette-knife contact and a short cohesive damp repair can be read together.
visual_priorities: The broken dry earthen surface, active blade contact and partly bridged wet seam explain cause, work and consequence in one frame.
Raw granular earth, crushed powder and damp filler remain visibly different material states with owners and spatial continuity.
The reference-guided face and short dark bob retain distinctive appearance while her attention makes the fragile repair matter.
The apron handprint and thumb smear stay attached to their actual carriers rather than becoming generic brown decoration.
baseline_prompt_en: An intimate documentary photograph of a woman with reference-guided face and hair in a soil-centered work scene. A restoration is in progress inside a small daylight atelier. She is seated at a scarred wooden bench, repairing an old ochre earthen-plaster relief panel that rests almost flat on a padded wooden support. One dry corner has flaked away, and the fallen matching chip lies beside it among angular clods and fine sandy earth. Her left palm steadies the sound outer edge of the panel; her right hand holds a short palette knife, its flat blade actually contacting the broken recess and pressing darker damp earth paste into it. Both forearms are visible and lead naturally back to her shoulders. A short part of the fissure is already bridged by a moist, slightly raised repair, while the remaining pale brittle fracture stays visible next to it. The place where the blade ends, the freshly filled section, and the unrepaired edge are all easy to distinguish. A shallow bowl of damp earthy paste sits within reach on the right side of the bench. In the foreground, a small mortar contains crushed ochre soil, and a wire sieve rests above a tray of powder, connecting raw earth to the repair. Soil is materially legible as granular powder, rough dry clods, and a cohesive wet patch, with tiny mineral grains visible in the old panel. A dusty rust-colored handprint marks the front of her oatmeal canvas apron, and a smear of the same wet earth clings to her right thumb beside the knife grip. Her visible oval face, large brown eyes, small straight nose, softly flushed cheeks and pink lips retain the supplied reference's proportions; her glossy dark chin-length bob and fine airy center-parted fringe retain its silhouette. She looks down toward the seam with a softened brow and gently parted lips, caught between concentration and relief as the material begins to hold. A simple cream sleeveless cotton top under the apron and loose hair framing her cheek give a quiet, intimate human warmth. A landscape three-quarter medium view from across the bench keeps her face, connected arms, apron transfer and repair on the same visual plane. Soft side window light rakes across the earthen surfaces; restrained ochre and cream tones, realistic pores and cotton fibers, moderate depth of field, an unhurried lived-in atelier impression.
